assumptions: Two server-owned preparation versions, two fields per batch, one initial committed version, and atomic SQL pointer publication. UUID uniqueness and provider create-only semantics are assumed; generic SQL/TypeScript refinement is not proved.

A successful field PUT acknowledges complete bytes. Provider failure can be ambiguous, and a sibling PUT can settle after its caller rejected. Prepared objects never replace the bytes of any old or concurrent version.

Failed and abandoned preparation objects are retained without speculative deletion. An unknown SQL outcome may still reference them. Crash orphan reclamation and durable cleanup receipts remain explicit unimplemented obligations; this model does not establish a garbage collector.

Existing trusted explicit R2 pointer restoration bypasses preparation and remains supported. Tenant authorization, same-row lifecycle/financial CAS, arbitrary content bytes, provider checksum verification and external corruption remain outside this bounded model.

The real PGlite tests cover four fields, rollback after PUT, parallel writers, ambiguous and rejected PUTs, late sibling settlement and retained-pointer restoration. They do not establish live R2/S3 qualification or database transport-ambiguous commit handling.
bounds.progress: Preparations and outstanding provider calls settle only under weak fairness of their provider/SQL continuations; no elapsed deadline, successful write or cleanup is guaranteed.

assumptions: Provider and SQL continuations are weakly fair. Success, crash recovery and orphan cleanup are not assumed.
